company_description: Uber Technologies, Inc. develops and operates proprietary technology applications in the United States, Canada, Latin America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Asia Pacific. The company operates through three segments: Mobility, Delivery, and Freight. The Mobility segment connects consumers with a range of transportation modalities, such as ridesharing, carsharing, micromobility, rentals, public transit, taxis, and other modalities; and offers riders in a variety of vehicle types, as well as financial partnerships products and advertising services. The Delivery segment allows consumers to search for and discover restaurants to grocery, alcohol, convenience, and other retailers, as well as order a meal or other items, and either pick-up at the restaurant or have it delivered; and provides Uber direct, a white-label delivery-as-a-service for retailers and restaurants, as well as advertising services. risks.title: Reclassification of drivers as employees
risks.summary: The classification of drivers as independent contractors is contested in many countries. Reclassification as employees would result in considerable costs (wages, benefits, taxes) and could fundamentally alter Uber's business model.
risks.score_rationale: This risk is mentioned first among risk factors and is detailed over several pages. The language used is strong ('material adverse effect', 'significant additional expenses'). This is a major risk to Uber's business model. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: High competitive intensity
risks.summary: The mobility, delivery, and logistics market is highly competitive with many well-established players and potential new entrants. Uber must constantly adjust its pricing and incentives to remain competitive.
risks.score_rationale: This risk is mentioned very early and is described as 'highly competitive' with 'low barriers to entry' and 'well-capitalized competitors'. The intensity of competition justifies a high severity rating. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Cybersecurity and data protection risks
risks.summary: Uber is exposed to cyberattacks and data breaches, which could harm its reputation, operations, and result in regulatory penalties.
risks.score_rationale: The text explicitly mentions 'security or privacy breaches' and 'Cyberattacks' with concrete examples. The potential impact on reputation and operations justifies a high severity rating. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Potential failure of autonomous vehicle technologies
risks.summary: Uber may fail to deploy autonomous vehicle technologies competitively or safely, which would affect its future growth strategy against competitors.
risks.score_rationale: This risk is related to a major strategic investment ('autonomous vehicle technologies'). Failure to compete or deploy these technologies at scale would have a significant impact. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Difficulty attracting and retaining platform users
risks.summary: The inability to attract and retain sufficient drivers, customers, and merchants could make the platform less attractive and harm growth.
risks.score_rationale: The risk of not maintaining a 'critical mass' of users (drivers, consumers, merchants) is highlighted as essential for platform attractiveness. Dependence on this critical mass is strong. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Regulatory risks and compliance
risks.summary: Uber is subject to complex and evolving regulations in many areas (payments, data, etc.), which can result in investigations, fines, and modifications to its business model.
risks.score_rationale: The document mentions 'numerous legal and regulatory risks' and 'extensive government regulation and oversight'. Fines, investigations, and legislative actions are recurring threats. (default score, to be refined)
